logline: When a failed drug triggers a bloodlust epidemic and quarantine seals a newly built apartment block, the residents of each floor discover that surviving the outbreak is only the second most dangerous thing happening inside the building.

bollymeter.basis: The IMDb 7.7 from a broad international audience reflects a show that delivered on its contained premise without transcending it. A sleeper-hit trajectory on Netflix Global Top 10 in April 2022 confirmed that word-of-mouth quality outlasted its modest original broadcast ratings.

pull_quotes.text: This is the zombie show that I didn't know I needed in my life.

seasons.review_body: Happiness aired on tvN from November to December 2021 and took an original angle on the Korean zombie genre: instead of setting the outbreak in open society, it quarantined an entire apartment building and used that closed system to examine class and real estate anxiety alongside survival horror. A failed pharmaceutical called Next triggers the Lytta Virus, producing short bouts of bloodlust in the infected. Han Hyo-joo as an immune police officer and Park Hyung-sik as her contract-husband detective are the central pair, and critics and audiences both pointed to their chemistry as the show's most reliable pleasure. The series became a sleeper hit when it arrived on Netflix's global platform in April 2022 - reaching number seven on the non-English Weekly Top 10 - suggesting that its modest original tvN ratings understated actual audience appetite. The IMDb score of 7.7 reflects a genre show that executes its premise cleanly without reaching for the allegorical depth of contemporaries like Squid Game.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Happiness Episode 1 aired November 5, 2021 on tvN and established the series' structural premise with precision: the apartment building as a pressure cooker before the Lytta Virus was confirmed, with class tensions between floor-level residents doing as much narrative work as the outbreak mechanics. Director Ahn Gil-ho's decision to ground the horror in the social architecture of the building - who gets which unit, what resources each floor controls, who already hates whom - gave the zombie premise a layered foundation that distinguished it from contemporaneous Korean genre entries. The Fangirl Verdict's assessment of the series as 'the zombie show I didn't know I needed in my life' accurately captures a premiere that arrives as a contained social thriller rather than a spectacle. Han Hyo-joo and Park Hyung-sik's chemistry is operational from their first shared scene, and the first infected resident in the stairwell is the episode's commitment point: the show declares its horror register without softening it.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere sets up the apartment building as a pressure cooker before the virus is even confirmed - the class tensions between residents already established through the politics of who gets which unit. The outbreak escalation in the final act is earned by this groundwork.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first infected resident in the stairwell - the moment the show commits to its horror register and does not look away.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 12
episode_reviews.review_body: Happiness Episode 12 aired December 11, 2021 on tvN as the series finale and resolved both the outbreak and the central romantic arc simultaneously, maintaining the show's conviction that the human threats inside the quarantine perimeter were always more interesting than what was outside it. Han Hyo-joo and Park Hyung-sik's performance chemistry, which The Fangirl Verdict identified as the series' most reliable pleasure, reaches its most direct expression in the finale's closing minutes. The IMDb audience score of 7.7 reflects a genre show that executed its contained premise cleanly without overextending the twelve-episode format. The Netflix global platform arrival in April 2022 - which pushed Happiness to number seven on the weekly non-English Top 10 - confirmed that the finale's word-of-mouth quality outlasted its modest original broadcast ratings on tvN.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves the central romantic arc and the outbreak in parallel, with the series maintaining its conviction that the human threat inside the quarantine perimeter was always more interesting than what was outside it. The closing image is more hopeful than the genre usually permits.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The couple's choice in the final minutes - a declaration that reframes their contract arrangement across the whole season.
